newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise on brisk fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise on brisk fund buying.

text.p: Aggressive buying by India's largest mutual fund, the Unit Trust of India (UTI), and foreign institutions drove Delhi shares higher in afternoon trade on Tuesday, brokers said.
At 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT), the Delhi Stock Exchange benchmark index was up 8.10 points to 905.89.
Traders attributed the surge to resumed buying by UTI after several days of remaining on the sidelines.
"Huge short-covering by bear operators, who made short-selling in the past several sessions, was another reason behind a rally in prices," said Suresh Aggarwal of stock brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Steel maker TISCO led the charge, climbing nine rupees to 200, fuelled by rumours that the firm will soon raise prices.
ITC Ltd rose one rupee to 556.
Associated Cement Companies Ltd gained 92.25 rupees to 1,523.
